alternatives_considered: Scale inline at the call site in the collection script
Raise the velocity limit so the difference becomes visible
A named, separately tested conversion function
claim_boundary: The conversion is correct for the GO Stanford metric spacing under the pinned reference configuration, verified against the upstream deployment constant.
correction: `unnormalise_waypoint(waypoint, *, metric_waypoint_spacing, waypoint_spacing=1)`, scaling only the x/y components and refusing non-positive or non-finite scales.
decision: Added `unnormalise_waypoint` to `src/navfm/control.py` as a named conversion with its own tests, and a test that asserts the concealment property itself.
decision_rule: When a safety mechanism can make a wrong value observationally identical to a right one, the conversion must be a named, independently tested unit -- because no integration test downstream of the clamp can ever discriminate.
impact: No published result depended on it: the affected pilots are SIMULATION_DEVELOPMENT and carry admission_status NOT_ADMITTED. Had it reached a training run, every action label in that run would have been wrong by a constant factor.
non_claim: This does not establish that the resulting velocities are correct for the physical Yahboom. The wheel radius remains a PROVISIONAL_SIMULATION_VALUE, so the metres are correct in simulation and unverified on hardware.
observation: ViNT waypoints were passed to the controller without being scaled by the dataset's metric spacing, making every commanded velocity roughly eight times too fast. The robot's motion looked plausible in both pilots.
propagation: Applies to every consumer of model waypoints: the collection script, the Navigation State panel's runtime, and any future deployment path. All three now route through the single named function.
regression_control: The concealment test fails if anyone removes the clamp or changes the limit, forcing a conscious decision rather than a silent change of detectability.
rejected_alternative: Raising the velocity limit to expose the error was rejected: it would trade a silent correctness bug for a real collision risk on hardware, and it fixes the detector rather than the defect.
root_cause: The model predicts waypoints in units of dataset waypoint spacing, not metres. The conversion is implicit in the reference deployment code and was not carried across as a named step, so there was no place for it to be absent from.
scientific_risk: Every collected trajectory would encode a control law eight times too aggressive, while remaining indistinguishable from correct data in the regime where the clamp is active. The error would surface only in slow manoeuvres, i.e. precisely the fine control a navigation claim rests on.
title: Waypoint un-normalisation missing; the safety clamp hid it
validation: 22 tests in `tests/test_vint_action_bridge.py`, including `test_saturation_HIDES_the_scale_error_at_realistic_magnitudes`, which asserts that correct and incorrect commands are equal after clamping -- the test exists to document why the bug was invisible, not merely to check the fix.
why_existing_checks_missed_it: The 0.45 m/s saturation limit returns an identical command for the correct 0.48 m/s and the wrong 4.0 m/s, because both exceed it. The safety limiter erased the difference before any assertion could see it. Every downstream artefact -- trajectory shape, pose log, image sequence -- was byte-identical under both the correct and the incorrect scaling.

alternatives_considered: Trust the importer's defaults
Assert on commanded velocity only
Compare commanded velocity against achieved displacement
claim_boundary: Establishes that the simulated robot moves under command in Isaac Sim 5.1 with the stated gains.
correction: Explicit wheel drive gains at articulation setup; ratio recorded per run.
decision: Set `kps=0, kds=1e4` on the wheel DOFs, and record the commanded-to-achieved ratio in every collection record.
decision_rule: A recording pipeline must assert on a physical quantity it did not command. Checking that the command was issued verifies the sender, not the world.
impact: Caught before any admitted data existed. The affected run was discarded; no downstream artefact consumed it.
non_claim: The ratio of ~1.1 is not a calibration result. It is an unexplained 10% overshoot that remains open, and it is not claimed that simulated dynamics match the physical robot.
observation: A pilot produced 40 perfectly-formed frames -- correct dtypes, contiguous images, aligned poses, unwrapped yaw -- of a robot that had moved 0.001 m while its own log reported a commanded 0.45 m/s.
propagation: Affects every trajectory collected in simulation. The ratio check now runs in the collection script and the Navigation State runtime.
regression_control: The ratio is written into every trajectory record, so a future zero-motion run is visible in the artefact rather than requiring someone to watch the viewport.
rejected_alternative: Asserting only on commanded velocity was rejected because that is the quantity the defect leaves intact -- it is the reason the failure was silent.
root_cause: The URDF importer created the wheel degrees of freedom with no drive gains. The articulation accepted velocity targets and applied no torque.
scientific_risk: A dataset of stationary observations labelled with non-zero actions. Training on it would teach the inverse of the intended mapping while every data-quality check reported healthy.
title: Wheel joints imported with zero stiffness and zero damping
validation: Commanded 0.450 m/s against achieved 0.491 and 0.505 m/s across two pilots (ratios 1.09 and 1.12), over paths of 4.867 m and 4.968 m.
why_existing_checks_missed_it: The output file satisfies every Option 1 format check and loads cleanly in all three models. Format validity and physical validity are independent properties, and only the first was being checked. Nothing in the schema can express 'the robot did not move'.

alternatives_considered: Report the aggregate 'parameters changed' count only
Treat 488/504 as within tolerance and move on
Name every unmoved tensor and trace each to upstream source
claim_boundary: A property of the released `vint.pth` and `nomad.pth` under the pinned reference architecture at commit dca7981, on a strict=True load.
correction: None applied to upstream. This is a finding about the distributed files, not a defect in our code; `parameters_unchanged` now carries names, counts and share.
decision: Record the exact tensor names, element counts and checkpoint fraction in the machine-readable result, and trace both causes to specific upstream lines.
decision_rule: 'Most parameters moved' is how a genuinely disconnected branch survives review. A proof that a training path is connected must be per-tensor or it is not a proof.
impact: No result is invalidated. Strict load still passes 3/3 and inference is unaffected. It changes arithmetic that gets published: ViNT's 29.7M parameters are 24.0M executed.
non_claim: Not a claim that the models were trained incorrectly. The prototype layer never participated in training either, so the released weights are exactly what the published procedure produced. It is a claim about what the files contain.
observation: In the train-path proof, 16 parameters of ViNT and the same 16 of NoMaD received no gradient and were unmoved by an optimizer step: 5,714,384 elements (19.21%, 22.9 MB fp32) for ViNT and 3,351,760 (17.59%, 13.4 MB) for NoMaD.
propagation: Affects any parameter count, memory estimate or optimizer configuration derived from these checkpoints, including our own fine-tuning plans and any figure quoting model size.
regression_control: The train-path harness fails if zero parameters move, and records the unmoved set every run, so a change in the dead set is visible as a diff.
rejected_alternative: Accepting 488/504 as good enough was rejected: the 16 are not a rounding error, they are a structural property of the released artefact, and the same reasoning would have hidden a real disconnection of identical size.
root_cause: Two independent upstream constructions. (a) `vint.py:41,46` read `obs_encoder._fc.in_features` and `goal_encoder._fc.in_features` as a shape lookup while the forward pass calls `extract_features`, so both EfficientNet classifier heads are carried and never called. (b) `self_attention.py:31-32` passes `self.sa_layer` to `nn.TransformerEncoder`, which deep-copies it -- verified directly, `enc.layers[0] is l` is False with no shared storage -- leaving the prototype layer registered, serialised, and unexecuted.
scientific_risk: Published parameter counts read off the checkpoint overstate the trainable model by ~19%, fine-tuning budgets over-provision by the same fraction, and AdamW allocates optimizer moments for 5.7M tensors that never receive a gradient.
title: About 19% of the released ViNT checkpoint is never executed
validation: `gates/forensics/train_path_compatibility.json`; the deep-copy mechanism confirmed by direct object-identity and storage-pointer comparison rather than inferred from the documentation.
why_existing_checks_missed_it: Every existing check is satisfied by this state. Strict load compares key sets and the keys match on both sides. Inference compares outputs and the outputs are correct, because the dead tensors are not in the graph. A loss curve descends normally. Only a check that asks which specific tensors an optimizer step moved can see it, and that check existed only because the train-path proof needed to distinguish 'the backward pass ran' from 'the backward pass did something'.

alternatives_considered: Trust the parent prim's name
Assert on the measured world-space height
claim_boundary: The simulated camera is at 0.2800 m in the current twin, measured from the transform, not read from a name.
correction: Traversal-based resolution plus a measured-height assertion in acceptance.
decision: Resolve the mount by traversing for the link, and derive `mounted_on_top_arm` from measured height (> 0.15 m) rather than from the parent's name.
decision_rule: Assert on the physical quantity that matters, never on a label that is expected to correlate with it. Names are metadata; geometry is the claim.
impact: Empirically material: with start, goal, seed, policy and physics held fixed and the camera the only change, pilot_0002 yaw went from +8.8 deg to +37.9 deg.
non_claim: Not verified against the physical Yahboom's actual mast height. The URDF mast is a represented structure, not a measured one.
observation: After adding the top-arm mast to the URDF, acceptance reported a camera mounted on `top_arm_mount` while the camera was in fact at 0.120 m, chassis height.
propagation: Invalidated the earlier pilots as evidence of the corrected viewpoint. Those are retained as a separate camera-domain experiment rather than deleted, since they are evidence of the domain effect.
regression_control: The height assertion fails on any future build that re-flattens the hierarchy.
rejected_alternative: Name-based resolution was rejected outright -- it had already produced a false PASS twice.
root_cause: The URDF importer flattens the link hierarchy, making nominal children into siblings. The prim carrying the expected name was not at the expected place.
scientific_risk: Every trajectory would come from the wrong visual domain while the record asserted the corrected viewpoint -- a domain error certified as fixed.
title: Camera parented to a prim named top_arm_mount but sitting at chassis height
validation: Camera measured at 0.2800 m from ground, 0.2400 m above `base_link`. Acceptance correctly FAILED twice before the fix, which is the evidence that the check discriminates.
why_existing_checks_missed_it: The check asked whether the camera's parent was *named* `top_arm_mount`. Name is not geometry. The assertion was true and the configuration was wrong.

alternatives_considered: Compare summary metrics between runs
Verify the camera contract field before reading any result
claim_boundary: Applies to the audit procedure for collection artefacts.
correction: Stale pilots deleted; collection re-launched; contract read first.
decision: Verify the contract field first, before any other field, on every artefact.
decision_rule: When a run is supposed to change a condition, check the condition before checking the outcome. Identical outcomes are evidence of identical inputs at least as often as they are evidence of reproducibility.
impact: No admitted data affected; the error was in reading, and lasted minutes.
non_claim: Not a defect in the collection code itself.
observation: Two pilot directories were treated as products of the corrected camera build. Their `camera_prim` field read `base_link` and their mtimes were 30 minutes old.
propagation: Applies to every future re-collection where a condition is meant to change.
regression_control: Collection records now embed the camera contract, so a stale artefact is self-identifying.
rejected_alternative: Metric comparison across runs was rejected as the primary check: it is satisfied most strongly by exactly the failure it needs to catch.
root_cause: A collection run failed to overwrite, and the reading order started from the numeric results rather than from the contract fields.
scientific_risk: Chassis-camera data presented as top-arm data, with an apparent replication to support it.
title: Stale pilots reported as fresh output
validation: Fresh pilots carry the corrected `camera_prim` and the measured height.
why_existing_checks_missed_it: The numbers agreed to three decimal places with the previous run -- because they were the same files. Agreement was read as reproducibility.

alternatives_considered: Keep 0.048 m as upstream-sourced
Block all simulation work pending caliper measurement
Adopt 0.040 m marked PROVISIONAL_SIMULATION_VALUE
claim_boundary: A provisional simulation parameter, sourced and documented.
correction: 0.040 m in all nine places in the vendored URDF fork.
decision: Adopt 0.040 m, explicitly marked PROVISIONAL_SIMULATION_VALUE in the ledger.
decision_rule: Simulator engineering proceeds open-by-default on a documented, plausible, sourced value, provided the value is never claimed as measured and the marker travels with it.
impact: Affects all simulated velocities and displacements. No admitted result depends on it; every simulation artefact is NOT_ADMITTED.
non_claim: Not a measurement. 0.040 m has not been verified against the physical robot and must not be cited as a hardware specification.
observation: The upstream Yahboom URDF specifies wheel radius 0.048 m in nine places, with a comment reading 'same as X3'. The M3 Pro is not an X3.
propagation: Propagates to every kinematic quantity in simulation, and to the G1 physical measurement task which must resolve it.
regression_control: The PROVISIONAL marker blocks promotion of any physical claim until a measurement with a recorded method replaces it.
rejected_alternative: Blocking on calipers was rejected because it would halt simulation development over a parameter that no simulation-stage claim depends on; the marker carries the uncertainty instead.
root_cause: A value copied across robot models without re-measurement.
scientific_risk: A 20% error in every velocity and every recorded position, landing directly in the `position` array that becomes the action label.
title: Wheel radius inherited from a different robot
validation: Cross-repo forensic audit identified the same 0.048 error across three repositories; the URDF's own comment supplies the origin.
why_existing_checks_missed_it: It corrupts every commanded velocity and every odometry displacement by the same 20% factor. Uniform corruption passes every internal consistency check, because consistency is exactly what it preserves.

alternatives_considered: Fix defects as found
Re-adjudicate the whole document after every correction
claim_boundary: Concerns the adjudication of Amendment 5 and the protocol documents.
correction: Eight rounds; the eighth a four-lens panel with two skeptics per claim.
decision: Re-adjudicate the entire amendment after every correction round, until a round returns zero defects.
decision_rule: A correction is not complete until the document is re-read whole. Local edits to a document with redundant statements of fact are presumed incomplete.
impact: 22 defects caught before the amendment was committed. The finding is the pattern, not the individual defects.
non_claim: Not a claim that the resulting protocol is scientifically correct -- only that it is internally consistent and executable.
observation: Adjudication rounds 3 through 6 of Amendment 5 were each decided by the same class of defect: prose corrected in one place while a summary, preamble or adjacent sentence retained the superseded claim. Round 7's single defect was the same provenance claim ten lines above the sentence fixed in round 6.
propagation: Applies to every future amendment, and to the paper, where the same narrative-plus-summary structure recurs.
regression_control: Amendments are appended, never edited, and the frozen section is verified byte-identical with `cmp` after every write.
rejected_alternative: Fixing defects as found was rejected empirically: it produced rounds 5, 6 and 7, each surfacing a stale copy of a fact already corrected.
root_cause: A document with a narrative section and a summary section has two statements of every fact, and editing is naturally local.
scientific_risk: A pre-registration that authorises what its preamble forbids is unexecutable, and the reader follows whichever half they read. In round 4 the preamble forbade training while three steps authorised it.
title: Corrections that did not propagate — the dominant protocol defect
validation: Round 8 returned zero surviving defects. Iteration signature 4-6-3-3-2-3-1-0.
why_existing_checks_missed_it: Each individual correction was correct. No check compares a document against itself, and a reviewer reading for correctness reads the corrected passage.

alternatives_considered: Close G2 on the four recorded decisions
Record the fifth requirement as an explicit open item
claim_boundary: Concerns the G2 gate's scope and its tracking artefact.
correction: `gates/failures/F-G2-1.md`; the fifth requirement named in the open items.
decision: Filed as a failure record and surfaced as an open item requiring Frank's and Rui's decision. G2 remains open.
decision_rule: A gate closes on its stated condition, not on its tracking artefact. Where the two disagree, the condition wins and the artefact is the defect.
impact: No result affected; G2 has not closed and no experiment depends on it yet.
non_claim: Not a claim about the estimator's actual type-I behaviour, which is unmeasured.
observation: The G2 gate condition requires four design decisions together with the estimator's type-I error rate on simulated null data and its tolerance. `gates/g2_decisions.json` holds four entries.
propagation: Blocks the E2 decision pack until the null-simulation harness exists and its tolerance is declared in advance.
regression_control: G2 cannot be marked closed while the null-simulation harness is absent.
rejected_alternative: Closing on four was rejected: it would step over the fifth silently, which is the specific failure the record now exists to prevent.
root_cause: The tracking file was built from an enumeration of the design decisions and silently dropped the conjunctive fifth requirement.
scientific_risk: Closing G2 with four of five requirements met, and a type-I error rate that was never measured, on an estimator whose false-positive behaviour is the thing the gate exists to bound.
title: G2 mis-scoped in both directions
validation: The gate condition text and the tracking file compared directly.
why_existing_checks_missed_it: Four of four entries present reads as complete. Nothing compares the tracking file against the gate condition that defines it.

alternatives_considered: pip install einops into the training environment
Stage the dependency outside the environment and pass it on the path
claim_boundary: Concerns environment identity for the reproduction ladder evidence.
correction: `--extra-syspath` on the verification harnesses; nothing installed.
decision: Stage to `/tmp/navfm-r6-deps` with `pip install --target` and pass `--extra-syspath`. The environment is never modified.
decision_rule: Never mutate an environment whose identity is part of the evidence. Dependencies needed for verification are staged outside it and named explicitly at the call.
impact: Preserved the validity of G0.c, R6 and R7, all of which cite the environment digest.
non_claim: Not a claim that the staged `einops` version matches what upstream used; it is recorded, not verified against their environment.
observation: NoMaD's vendored diffusion policy requires `einops`, absent from the training environment. The obvious fix is `pip install einops`.
propagation: Applies to every verification harness that needs a dependency the environment lacks.
regression_control: The harnesses refuse to auto-discover interpreters or install anything, and name the missing requirement instead (the F-M1-1 rule).
rejected_alternative: Installing was rejected because the cost is invisible: it does not fail, it quietly changes what the audit is about.
root_cause: Environment identity is defined by a digest over the pip freeze output, so any install changes the identity of the environment under audit.
scientific_risk: The G0.c freeze audit would certify an environment digest that no artefact was actually produced under, silently invalidating the reproducibility chain it exists to establish.
title: Installing a dependency would have broken the freeze audit before it ran
validation: Environment identity `4408691cfeb89860...` unchanged across the entire session, verified before and after the NoMaD work.
why_existing_checks_missed_it: Nothing would have failed. The install succeeds, NoMaD builds, the audit runs -- and reports on an environment that no longer matches the one whose identity was recorded. The check would have passed while measuring the wrong thing.

alternatives_considered: Delete the erroneous result
Annotate it in place with the category error
claim_boundary: Concerns the freeze audit's temporal scope.
correction: Annotation recording the category error alongside the original output.
decision: Annotate in place. The wrong result and its correction both stay in the record.
decision_rule: Erroneous results produced by this work are annotated, never deleted. A record that shows only correct conclusions cannot be audited for how it reached them.
impact: No result affected. The finding is about how audits are scoped and retained.
non_claim: Not a claim that the two flagged items were correct -- they were out of scope.
observation: A freeze audit run post-hoc reported '2 of 16 FAILED', which was recorded and then found to be a category error: the audit checks conditions that hold before execution, and it was run afterwards.
propagation: Applies to every gate script with a temporal precondition.
regression_control: The precondition is now stated in the audit's own output.
rejected_alternative: Deletion was rejected: it would leave a clean record that misrepresents the process, and remove the evidence that the audit needs a temporal precondition.
root_cause: The audit's temporal precondition was not encoded in the audit.
scientific_risk: Either a false alarm that discards valid evidence, or -- the worse direction -- a post-hoc pass read as a pre-execution guarantee.
title: A pre-execution gate audit run after execution, reported as failure
validation: The freeze audit's valid scope stated explicitly in the archived record.
why_existing_checks_missed_it: The audit produced a well-formed result with a plausible failure count. Nothing in the output indicates when it was valid to run.

alternatives_considered: Assert that 29 is expected from the arithmetic
Patch upstream so all three yield 30
Trace every candidate index through the pinned source and prove the rule
claim_boundary: Holds for the pinned upstream at dca7981 with waypoint_spacing 1 and end_slack 0. The rule is general; the specific counts are for a 40-frame trajectory.
correction: None needed. Classified DESIGN / MODEL-SEMANTIC, not defect and not off-by-one.
decision: Preserve 29. Emit a per-candidate index trace (`gates/forensics/nomad_sample_index_trace.csv`) and per-model population files asserting candidate = accepted + rejected, with the accepted set compared against the rule's range.
decision_rule: Scientific comparability means the same evidence standard, not identical internal implementation. A model-semantic difference is preserved and documented; it is never normalised away to make a table symmetrical.
impact: No result changes. The population difference is now a documented property of NoMaD's contract rather than an unexplained number, and any future three-model table must state it.
non_claim: Not a claim that 29 and 30 samples give equivalent statistical power, nor that the three models can be compared on equal footing without accounting for the population difference.
observation: On the same 40-frame Yahboom pilot, the three official dataset classes yielded GNM 30, ViNT 30, NoMaD 29 samples. The number was recorded before it was understood.
propagation: Applies to every dataset built for these three models and to any table reporting sample counts across them.
regression_control: The harness computes the predicted count from each config and asserts it against `len(dataset)` and against the accepted index set. A horizon change moves the count and the assertion reports it.
rejected_alternative: Forcing 30 was rejected because it would invent a sample outside NoMaD's admissible range and make the comparison less valid, not more. Asserting '29 is expected' from arithmetic alone was also rejected -- the arithmetic had to be shown to be the arithmetic the source actually performs.
root_cause: Model-specific sampling semantics, traced to `vint_dataset.py::_build_index` L219-221: `begin_time = context_size * waypoint_spacing`, `end_time = traj_len - end_slack - len_traj_pred * waypoint_spacing`, and every value in `range(begin_time, end_time)` is appended. There is no rejection branch in the source. GNM and ViNT use context 5 / horizon 5 giving range [5,35) = 30; NoMaD uses context 3 / horizon 8 giving range [3,32) = 29. The accepted index set was verified to equal the rule's range exactly for all three models.
scientific_risk: Two opposite errors. Treating 29 as a defect and patching upstream to force 30 would fabricate a sample NoMaD's contract does not admit. Treating it as noise would leave a population difference undocumented in any comparison across the three models.
title: NoMaD produces 29 samples where GNM and ViNT produce 30
validation: Exact answer: NoMaD *gains* candidate indices [3, 4] at the front, because it needs only 3 context frames against 5, and *loses* [32, 33, 34] at the back, because it predicts 8 steps ahead against 5. Net -1. No sample is silently lost; conservation holds for all three (40 = 30 + 10, 40 = 30 + 10, 40 = 29 + 11).
why_existing_checks_missed_it: Nothing was wrong, so nothing fired. Loader acceptance asks whether a dataset opens; it has no opinion about how many samples it should contain. The risk was not a failed check but an unexplained number sitting in a results table, where it would eventually be read as either a defect or a licence to force symmetry.

alternatives_considered: Keep the simplified loss and note it as an approximation
Import or transcribe the pinned implementation for every model
claim_boundary: The losses now executed are upstream's, at dca7981, for a single batch on CPU.
correction: Harness rewritten against pinned source; `_compute_losses_nomad` explicitly identified as the eval/logging path (it runs full diffusion sampling) and therefore NOT the training objective.
decision: GNM and ViNT now call upstream `_compute_losses` directly. NoMaD's training loss has no callable -- it is inline in `train_nomad` -- so it is transcribed line-for-line with its source range recorded, including `get_delta`, `normalize_data` against `ACTION_STATS`, the real DDPM scheduler configured as in `train.py` L214-219, goal masking, and both masked reductions.
decision_rule: A compatibility proof must exercise the implementation it claims compatibility with. Where upstream exposes a callable, call it. Where it does not, transcribe it and record the source range so the transcription can be audited.
impact: No published result affected -- the flawed harness existed for one iteration and was replaced before commit. Caught by review, not by any check in this repository, which is itself the finding.
non_claim: Not a claim that upstream's objective is scientifically correct. Conformance to a reference is not correctness of the reference.
observation: The first version of the train-path harness reported PASS for all three models. Its NoMaD objective was hand-written: `noisy = actions + noise * 0.1` with a plain MSE, no delta computation, no normalisation, no DDPM scheduler, no goal mask, no masked reduction. GNM and ViNT used a plain MSE in place of upstream's masked `action_reduce`.
propagation: Applies to every harness that claims to exercise an official path: evaluation, fine-tuning, and any future baseline reproduction.
regression_control: `gates/forensics/training_path_crosswalk.json` pins file, function and line range for every element of each model's training path, so a future drift from upstream is a diff rather than a discovery.
rejected_alternative: Noting the simplification as an approximation was rejected: the claim being made is specifically about the official path, so an approximation of it is not a weaker version of the claim but a different claim wearing its name.
root_cause: The harness was written to demonstrate that a gradient could flow, and a loss that produces a gradient is trivial to write. Reaching for the pinned implementation is a strictly harder path with an identical-looking result.
scientific_risk: A claim that our data survives the official training path, evidenced by a path that was not the official one. It would have been wrong in the specific way that is hardest to detect later: the artefact is well-formed, the numbers are finite, and the label on the box is the only thing that is false.
title: An invented loss passed the first train-path harness
validation: All three PASS on the official losses. GNM total 0.104939, ViNT 0.084481, NoMaD 0.036361, with NoMaD's stochastic state frozen and recorded (timesteps, noise digest, goal mask).
why_existing_checks_missed_it: Every check passed, and passed honestly: the losses were finite, the gradients were non-zero, the parameters moved. Nothing in a train-path proof can distinguish the real objective from a plausible one, because both make `backward()` work. Only reading the pinned source distinguishes them.

alternatives_considered: Assert that backward() raised no exception
Assert on the aggregate count of changed parameters
Record per-tensor deltas, and name every tensor that did not move
claim_boundary: Establishes that one optimizer step measurably updates the in-memory model for each of the three architectures on this data.
correction: Per-tensor gradient and parameter-delta audit in the harness.
decision: Measure and record: parameters with gradients, with non-zero gradients, with NaN gradients, with Inf gradients, the global gradient norm, per-tensor before/after norms and digests for a watched set, and the full name list of every tensor the step did not move.
decision_rule: Verify the effect, never the invocation. This applies system-wide: commanded velocity against achieved displacement, optimizer step against parameter delta, camera mount name against measured height.
impact: Turned a proof that a function was called into a proof that the model changed. Also produced FL-003, which only this check could surface.
non_claim: Not a claim that training would converge, that the updates are in a useful direction, or that the data is admissible for training.
observation: A train-path proof can call `backward()` and `optimizer.step()` and return cleanly while most of the intended network receives no useful gradient. In this run, 16 of ViNT's 504 trainable tensors and 16 of NoMaD's 644 received no gradient at all.
propagation: The rule applies to every actuation-like operation in the system, simulated, numerical or physical.
regression_control: The harness returns FAIL if zero parameters change, if any gradient is NaN or Inf, or if no parameter receives a non-zero gradient.
rejected_alternative: An aggregate count was rejected because 'most of them moved' is exactly how a genuinely disconnected branch survives review -- and it would have concealed the 16 dead tensors that turned out to be a real property of the released checkpoints (FL-003).
root_cause: The invocation and the effect are different events, and only the invocation is observable without extra work. This is the same class as the Yahboom commanding 0.45 m/s while moving 0.001 m.
scientific_risk: Certifying that data can train a model when in fact the training path is partially or wholly disconnected -- with a well-formed evidence file to support it.
title: optimizer.step() returning is not evidence the model changed
validation: GNM 324/326 non-zero gradients and 326/326 changed; ViNT 486/504 and 488/504; NoMaD 628/644 and 628/644. Zero NaN and zero Inf gradients across all three. The excess of changed over non-zero-gradient tensors is AdamW's decoupled weight decay acting on zero-gradient parameters, which is expected.
why_existing_checks_missed_it: There was no earlier check. A harness that asserts 'no exception raised' is satisfied by a completely disconnected model, because a zero gradient is not an error condition.

alternatives_considered: Rely on the smoke test not containing a save call
Copy checkpoints to a scratch location before testing
Hash the released file before and after and require equality
claim_boundary: Concerns the released checkpoint files during train-path smoke testing.
correction: Before/after SHA-256 on every checkpoint, per model, as a PASS condition.
decision: Hash each released checkpoint before and after every model's run and require equality. The model exists in memory only; no state is persisted.
decision_rule: Where an artefact is a fixed point of the evidence chain, immutability is asserted by measurement on every run that touches it -- never inferred from the absence of a write in the code.
impact: Preserves the validity of R6, R7 and G0.c, all of which cite checkpoint digests.
non_claim: Not a claim that the checkpoints match upstream's originally published files; that is R5's separate result.
observation: The train-path proof loads released weights and runs an optimizer step. Nothing in that sequence inherently prevents a save path from writing back to `checkpoints/*.pth`, and the resulting file would still load.
propagation: Applies to every future harness that loads released weights, including fine-tuning and evaluation.
regression_control: The check is a PASS condition of the harness, so any future write fails the run rather than being noticed later.
rejected_alternative: Relying on the absence of a save call was rejected because it is a property of the current code rather than of the artefact, and it silently stops holding the first time someone adds checkpointing to the harness.
root_cause: Checkpoint files are the reproduction chain's fixed point -- R6 strict load, R7 determinism and G0.c all cite their digests -- and the smoke test is the first code in the repository that both reads them and mutates a model.
scientific_risk: Silent invalidation of R6, R7 and G0.c: their evidence cites digests that would no longer correspond to the file on disk, and the reproduction ladder would rest on an artefact modified by an engineering test.
title: A training smoke test could quietly mutate a released checkpoint
validation: `checkpoint_unchanged: true` for all three models across all runs, with both digests recorded in each artefact.
why_existing_checks_missed_it: A mutated checkpoint is a valid checkpoint. It loads strictly, produces finite outputs, and passes every structural check. Only a digest comparison against the recorded value can see it, and the digest would have been recomputed from the mutated file if it were re-recorded.

alternatives_considered: Pitch the camera down to reduce the black region
Lower the camera back toward chassis height
Diagnose the optical axis analytically, then test the world
claim_boundary: The optical axis is forward and level, established analytically from the USD transform and confirmed by rendered composition in two worlds.
correction: No camera change. Two-tier scene policy introduced, with the control world retained for physics and regression and explicitly barred from navigation claims.
decision: Keep the top-arm mount and the optical axis unchanged. Classify the sparse world as ENGINEERING_CONTROL_WORLD and source a real Isaac USD environment for navigation pilots.
decision_rule: Before altering a component to fix an observation, establish that the component is the cause. Here the optical axis was computable in closed form and turned out to be exactly correct.
impact: Prevented a change to the camera mount that would have degraded the viewpoint and invalidated comparison with the existing pilots.
non_claim: Not a claim that 0.280 m, the mast geometry or the 18 mm focal length match the physical Yahboom. All remain PROVISIONAL_SIMULATION_VALUE.
observation: Robot POV frames from pilot_0001 and pilot_0002 are dominated by black empty space above and floor below, with a few untextured primitives. The natural reading is that the camera is aimed wrongly and needs pitching down.
propagation: Scene identity now belongs in the same versioned contract as the camera: both are part of the data-generating process, and a change to either changes the observation distribution.
regression_control: `scripts/camera_view_acceptance.py` measures composition from the depth buffer on every scene, so a viewpoint regression is a number rather than an opinion.
rejected_alternative: Pitching down was rejected on measurement: at 0.280 m with a 47.2 degree vertical field, downward pitch increases floor fraction, which is already 41% in the control world.
root_cause: The camera is correct. Its USD rotation (90, 0, -90) maps the camera's -Z view direction onto the robot's +X with +Z up, giving optical axis [1, 0, 0], pitch 0.0 deg, and intrinsics of 60.4 x 47.2 degrees -- comparable to a RealSense D435. The world is the defect: a 40 m ground plane and one distant light in an unbounded void, with no walls, no ceiling and no sky dome. With the camera level at 0.280 m the horizon falls on the image centre, so the upper half of every frame is rays terminating in nothing (black) and the lower half is floor.
scientific_risk: Pitching the camera down to 'fix' the black region would have traded void for more floor, degrading the viewpoint while appearing to address the complaint -- and would have silently changed the mount geometry that the +8.8 to +37.9 degree yaw experiment established as behaviourally significant.
title: The poor navigation images were the world, not the camera
validation: Same robot, same camera, same intrinsics, rendered in both worlds: background fraction 33% in the control world against 0% in a bounded interior, and median forward depth 1.65 m against 8.99 m. The camera never changed.
why_existing_checks_missed_it: The camera acceptance test asked whether the camera was mounted at the right height on the right link and pointing forward. All three were true. No check asked what the camera could see, because scene content was not modelled as part of the camera contract at all.

alternatives_considered: Trust the closure manifest's completeness flag
Collect anyway and note the appearance caveat
Audit the stage directly and block on the defect
claim_boundary: Concerns the two local mirrors at their current state on this machine, audited in-stage under Isaac Sim 5.1.0.0.
correction: In-stage eligibility audit; manifest records `closure_flag_disagrees_with_audit: true` for both scenes.
decision: Both scenes marked NOT eligible. `scripts/audit_scene_assets.py` opens each stage, counts referenced MDL modules against files on disk, and the manifest takes eligibility from that audit rather than from the closure flag.
decision_rule: A provenance manifest is evidence about what a tool looked for, never proof of what an asset contains. Eligibility is decided by inspecting the loaded stage.
impact: Blocks navigation-pilot collection until materials are obtained. No data was collected in either scene, so no artefact is contaminated.
non_claim: Not a claim that the upstream NVIDIA assets are incomplete. The defect is in the local mirroring, not necessarily in the source.
observation: The hospital and warehouse mirrors both record `closure_complete: true` with zero unresolved references -- 293 and 53 files respectively, each with a digest. Loading the hospital renders a uniformly red frame. There are zero `.mdl` files on disk in either mirror, against 10 and 13 MDL modules referenced.
propagation: Applies to every mirrored asset produced by the same closure tool, in this repository and in the sibling robotics repositories that share the mirror.
regression_control: `build_scene_manifest.py` refuses to mark a scene eligible without an audit on record, and defaults to not eligible when none exists.
rejected_alternative: Collecting with an appearance caveat was rejected: appearance is the entire input to a visual navigation model, so a caveat would not scope the defect, it would only label it.
root_cause: The closure walker followed USD-to-USD references to a fixed point but did not follow MDL material-module references. Materials are referenced by a different mechanism, so they were never enumerated and their absence was never noticed.
scientific_risk: Collecting a 'photorealistic hospital' dataset whose observation distribution is flat fallback colour. Every geometric property would be right and every appearance property wrong, and the resulting data would look like a valid indoor navigation corpus.
title: Asset mirrors report a complete closure while missing every material module
validation: hospital_v1: 10 MDL modules referenced, 0 on disk. simple_warehouse_v1: 13 referenced, 0 on disk. Both eligible=false. The rendered hospital frame has 96% of its saturated pixels in a single hue bucket.
why_existing_checks_missed_it: Every check upstream of the renderer succeeds. The stage opens, 1917 prims load, geometry is present, the camera renders, depth is finite and plausible. The closure manifest is not merely silent about the problem -- it positively asserts completeness, which is worse than saying nothing.

alternatives_considered: Keep the geometric metrics and rely on human review for appearance
Tighten the threshold and add appearance metrics, then prove both directions
claim_boundary: The corrected check discriminates between these two defect classes on these fixtures.
correction: Thresholds recalibrated against measurement and recorded as recalibrated; two appearance metrics added.
decision: Tighten `background_fraction_max` from 0.35 to 0.10 against measured data, add dominant-hue and colour-diversity metrics, and re-run against both known-bad frames to confirm each is rejected for its own reason.
decision_rule: A verification must be shown to fail when its subject is defective, using a real defective input, before its passes are trusted.
impact: No collected data affected -- the check had certified nothing before it was corrected. Second instance this session of a green check that was wrong, after FL-012.
non_claim: Not a claim that it detects every bad viewpoint. It is a floor, and the thresholds are engineering values recalibrated after seeing data, not pre-registered criteria.
observation: The first version of the camera-view acceptance test returned PASS for the control world's black void and PASS for the uniformly red hospital render. Both frames are rejected by a human on sight.
propagation: Applies to every acceptance gate written in this project: each needs a known-bad fixture it demonstrably rejects.
regression_control: Both known-bad frames are retained under `gates/scenes/views/` as the fixtures the check must keep rejecting.
rejected_alternative: Relying on human review for appearance was rejected: it is exactly the supplementary evidence the gate is supposed to make unnecessary at scale.
root_cause: Two errors. The background threshold was set at 0.35 by estimation before any measurement, and the control world reads 0.33 -- inside the limit by luck. And the metric set was entirely geometric, so a scene whose materials had all fallen back scored perfectly: background 0%, structure 53%, forward depth 8.99 m.
scientific_risk: A gate that certifies any viewpoint is worse than no gate, because it converts an open question into a recorded PASS.
title: The camera-view acceptance test passed both known-bad frames
validation: Control world now FAILS on background 33% > 10%. Hospital now FAILS on 96% of saturated pixels in one hue. Each fails for its actual defect, not incidentally.
why_existing_checks_missed_it: This was the check. Nothing sits above it. It was written to measure composition rather than to be shown failing, so it was never run against a frame that should fail -- the exact omission the standing instructions name as a recurring genus.

alternatives_considered: Trust FULL_RENDER_CLOSURE and proceed to collection
Treat the unchanged render as a caching artefact and re-run
Take the renderer's own compile errors as the independent oracle
claim_boundary: Concerns dependency discovery for instanced USD scenes under Isaac Sim 5.1.0.0.
correction: Traversal now uses `Usd.TraverseInstanceProxies` and walks `stage.GetPrototypes()` directly; relative paths resolve against the authoring layer rather than the root.
decision: Treat the MDL compiler's `could not find module` errors as the authority over the dependency walk, and fix the traversal to include instance proxies and every prototype explicitly. Recount: 69 modules and 252 textures, all present.
decision_rule: A repair must be verified by an oracle independent of the discovery that produced it. When the fix and its check share an enumeration, the check confirms the enumeration, not the fix.
impact: No data collected under the false completeness. It converts FL-016 from a small gap into an order-of-magnitude error: the original mirror was not missing 10 files but 321, while asserting completeness throughout.
non_claim: Complete closure is not a claim that the scene renders correctly. Whether 321/321 clears the hue collapse is a separate gate and was unresolved when this entry was written.
observation: After fetching the 10 MDL modules the dependency walk reported as missing, the mirror recorded FULL_RENDER_CLOSURE true with zero unresolved, and the scene rendered exactly as before -- still hue-collapsed, byte-identical composition. The repair verified itself as complete while changing nothing observable.
propagation: Applies to every mirrored asset produced by the same walk, and to any audit whose completeness check reuses the enumeration under test.
regression_control: The mirror manifest records referenced counts per class, so a future traversal regression appears as a drop in what is asked for rather than as a clean pass.
rejected_alternative: Accepting FULL_RENDER_CLOSURE was rejected because the render had not changed. An unchanged observable after a repair claimed complete is evidence against the claim, not an anomaly to explain away.
root_cause: `Usd.Stage.Traverse()` does not descend into instance prototypes. These scenes are heavily instanced: most walls and doors live under `/__Prototype_*`. The walk therefore enumerated 10 material modules and 20 textures where the scene actually requires 69 and 252 -- it was hiding roughly 85% of the material graph. Both the original closure manifest and my repair used that same walk, so the repair's completeness check asked the identical narrowed question and got the identical reassuring answer.
scientific_risk: A scene certified render-complete, collected in, and published as a photorealistic interior while the majority of its materials never resolved. Every provenance field would be present and correct, and the observation distribution would still be wrong.
title: A repair verified by the same defective discovery that caused the fault
validation: Referenced counts moved from 10 to 69 MDL modules and 20 to 252 textures, with 321/321 present and zero unresolved, reproduced across two independent runs.
why_existing_checks_missed_it: The completeness check and the discovery step shared an implementation. A verification derived from the same enumeration as the fix cannot detect an enumeration fault -- it will report success precisely when the enumeration is wrong in the same way for both. The MDL compiler was the only component with an independent view, and its errors were being read as noise.

alternatives_considered: Add liveness assertions to each gate individually
Require reviewers to check that a run produced output
Make liveness part of the measurement's type, enforced at construction
claim_boundary: The type is in place with tests. Migration of the gates is staged: scene load, render, dependency audit, training smoke and evaluation first.
correction: Envelope type with `require_evidence()` that raises rather than returning a value, `not_run()` for the honest empty case, and pessimistic liveness defaults so a forgotten field yields NOT_RUN rather than a silent pass.
decision: `src/navfm/measurement.py`: a `MeasurementEnvelope` carrying liveness, value and provenance together. It refuses at construction to hold a value while liveness is incomplete, and reports RUN_LIVE_NO_MEASUREMENT rather than MEASURED_ZERO when the examined population is empty. Status is five-valued -- NOT_RUN, RUN_FAILED, RUN_LIVE_NO_MEASUREMENT, MEASURED_ZERO, MEASURED_NONZERO -- because the four ways of lacking an answer need different responses and a boolean collapses them into the one that resembles success.
decision_rule: MEASUREMENT = LIVENESS + VALUE + PROVENANCE, never MEASUREMENT = VALUE. A reported zero is a conclusion only after liveness is established; otherwise it is missing evidence wearing the appearance of success. Null execution and zero outcome must never share a representation.
impact: No published result rested on one of the three: the closure repair was caught by an unchanged render, the inert job by an empty output file, the unloaded scene by a REFUSED line. All three were caught by observation, none by a check.
non_claim: Not a claim that existing gates already emit envelopes. Until a gate is migrated, its zeros carry the same ambiguity described here.
observation: Three times in one session a null result was read as a clean one. A `pgrep -f` wait loop matched its own wrapper's command line, so a background job waited a day, ran nothing and wrote a 0-byte file while every status check said 'in progress'. A closure repair reported FULL_RENDER_CLOSURE true using the same traversal that caused the defect. And a scene test reported `mdl_error_count = 0` because its preflight had refused the URL and exited before Isaac started.
propagation: Applies to every gate in the repository and to future safety metrics, where the failure mode is worst -- a stationary robot produces a perfect collision record.
regression_control: `value` is refused at construction when liveness is incomplete, so a gate cannot emit a bare number without the proof that it measured anything.
rejected_alternative: Per-gate liveness assertions and reviewer discipline were both rejected: this failure occurred three times in one session inside an audit explicitly built around the declared-versus-observed distinction. Intent is demonstrably not the control; the type is.
root_cause: Measurements were represented as bare values. A value carries no record of whether the machinery that produces it ever ran, so `0` from a live measurement and `0` from an inert one are the same token. Every consumer then reads the second as the first, because that is the reading that requires no further work.
scientific_risk: The general form is severe. `0 collisions` from a robot that never moved, `0 invalid rows` from a validator over an empty input, `0 NaN gradients` from a backward pass that did not run -- each is a safety or correctness claim supported by an absence of observation rather than an observation of absence.
title: A zero produced by a run that never started, reported as a clean result
validation: 28 tests, each of the three incidents encoded as a case that must not pass: a scene that never loaded, a job that never ran, and a validator over an empty population. A stationary robot is asserted not to prove zero collisions.
why_existing_checks_missed_it: There was nothing to miss: the artefacts were well-formed and their values were the values a healthy run produces. Detection requires a fact the artefact did not carry -- whether the measurement executed over a non-empty population. No amount of care applied to the value can recover it.

alternatives_considered: Require all scenes to be local files
Validate by addressing scheme, deferring URI existence to the runtime resolver
claim_boundary: Concerns scene addressing in the acceptance gate under Isaac Sim 5.1.0.0.
correction: Scheme detection in the preflight, with the incident recorded at the call site.
decision: Detect the scheme and validate with the resolver appropriate to it: filesystem for local paths, the Omniverse runtime for URIs. URI existence is never tested with `Path.is_file()`.
decision_rule: An identifier is validated by the resolver that owns its namespace. A check that cannot succeed for a valid input is not a strict check, it is a broken one.
impact: Established that the native resolver handles the full USD, MDL and texture graph correctly, and that the hand-built mirror was the defect rather than the assets.
non_claim: Not a claim that the Office scene is eligible. That run FAILED its own gate on background fraction, and the metric cannot yet distinguish an unbounded void from a legitimate view through a window.
observation: `camera_view_acceptance.py` preflighted its scene argument with `Path(args.scene).is_file()`. Given an Omniverse asset URL that is always false, so the script printed REFUSED and exited -- and the surrounding measurement reported zero MDL errors for a scene that had never been opened.
propagation: Applies to every script taking a scene or asset argument, and retires the local mirror as the acquisition path.
regression_control: The gate now reports whether an artefact was written alongside its error count, so a refused run cannot present as a clean one.
rejected_alternative: Requiring local files was rejected: it is what forced the hand-built mirror, which produced FL-016 and FL-018 and never resolved MDL correctly.
root_cause: Local filesystem paths and remote asset URIs were treated as one namespace. They are different addressing schemes with different resolvers, and only one of them answers `is_file()`.
scientific_risk: Any scene addressed by URI would be silently excluded from evaluation while the run reported a clean result -- and the native asset root is the correct way to reference these scenes, so the defect specifically blocked the working path.
title: A URL validated as a filesystem path, refused before anything ran
validation: With the fix, the Office scene loads from the asset root: 4713 prims, 140 meshes, 121 lights, 185 materials, zero MDL errors and zero error lines -- against 138 MDL errors from the local mirror.
why_existing_checks_missed_it: The preflight behaved exactly as designed and its refusal was printed. The defect was that the refusal was invisible to the measurement wrapped around it, which counted error lines in output that was never produced.

alternatives_considered: Loosen the threshold until Office passes
Exclude the upper image region from the background measurement
Split the observable into four classes and reject on true void alone
claim_boundary: Establishes that Office's apparent background is distant geometry and sky rather than void, at two audited poses under Isaac Sim 5.1.0.0.
correction: `scripts/scene_visibility_classification.py`, emitting MeasurementEnvelope.
decision: Classify every pixel as NEAR_SCENE, DISTANT_SCENE, VALID_ENVIRONMENT_BACKGROUND or TRUE_VOID, and move the rejection criterion onto true void. DISTANT_SCENE is established by an independent probe -- a second camera parented to the same link with identical intrinsics, differing only in far clip, which is set from the measured stage diagonal rather than chosen. The threshold stays at 0.10.
decision_rule: A threshold cannot repair a semantically wrong observable. Missing depth within a sensor's range is not equivalent to absence of scene geometry, and negative evidence requires proof that the observable was capable of seeing the thing claimed absent.
impact: No scene was selected under the wrong metric, and no data collected. Office's original rejection is now demonstrated to have been a false negative rather than assumed to be one.
non_claim: Not a claim that Office is eligible. Only two poses were measured, no corridor or goal-style viewpoint, and the material, hue, structure and depth checks have not yet been run through this gate. The environment-background rule is also currently coarse: every unexplained pixel is forgiven whenever the stage has any dome light, so a scene with a dome could in principle launder a real void. That is a known weakness, not a validated criterion.
observation: After `background_fraction_max` was tightened from 0.35 to 0.10 to stop the control world passing, the Office scene failed on 33.9% background -- while rendering a legible interior with carpet, a structural pillar and a window wall, under 185 correctly resolved materials and zero runtime errors.
propagation: Applies to every scene that will ever be audited, and to any future metric where sensor range limits are mistaken for absence -- including collision clearance and goal visibility.
regression_control: The control-world frame is retained as a negative fixture that must keep failing on true void while Office must not, so a future change collapsing the classes breaks one of the two.
rejected_alternative: Loosening the threshold until Office passed was rejected outright: it tunes the gate to the candidate in front of it, and would have left the metric unable to distinguish a void from a window in every future scene. Masking the upper image region was rejected for the same reason -- it hides the disagreement rather than resolving it.
root_cause: The observable was semantically wrong, not badly calibrated. It asked 'how many pixels have no depth return inside the canonical 100 m clip?' while the scientific question was 'how much of the forward view is genuinely an unbounded, non-environment void?'. Those are different estimands. A window onto a city skyline beyond the far clip scored identically to the control world's black nothing.
scientific_risk: Rejecting every architecturally realistic environment -- offices, warehouses and hospitals all have windows and openings -- and thereby selecting a canonical world biased toward sealed, windowless geometry for a reason having nothing to do with navigation.
title: Tightening a threshold fixed a false positive and created a false negative
validation: Control world, the discriminating case: true void 0.3894, distant scene 0.0, still FAIL -- the classifier does not rescue a genuine void, because DISTANT can only be earned by a positive observation. Office pose A decomposes its 33.9% background into 8.7% distant scene and 25.3% environment dome with 0.000 true void; pose B facing inward is 100% near scene. The class mask shows blue aligning with the skyline buildings and yellow with the sky above them.
why_existing_checks_missed_it: The metric was doing exactly what it was written to do, and its first recalibration was driven by a scene where the two estimands happened to coincide -- in an unbounded void, missing depth really is void. The divergence only appears in a bounded scene with a window, which is the case the metric was never tested against.
